Droll

DROHL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Droll is unusual in a way that is amusing.

The professor's droll asides were the only thing that kept students awake during the lecture.

Worked Example

The professor's droll observation about faculty meetings drew a few knowing chuckles from colleagues.

Droll describes a dry, understated, playfully quaint kind of humor -- more a wry smile than loud laughter.

How Droll Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

wry

wry: using dry, ironic humor

quaint

quaint: attractively unusual or old-fashioned

Antonyms

humorless

humorless: lacking any sense of humor

solemn

solemn: formal and serious

How Strong Is It? — amusing → droll → side-splitting

amusing vs. droll

amusing vs. droll: Something amusing simply entertains; something droll entertains in a specifically dry, understated way.

side-splitting vs. droll

side-splitting vs. droll: Side-splitting humor provokes loud, uncontrollable laughter, a far louder register than quiet, droll wit.
